example.output: clone has same adjacency but entirely new node identities
example.explanation: A map connects each original node to its unique clone.

constraints: Follow the linked problem's input constraints and node definitions; verify edge cases as part of practice.
solutions.approach: Explain the invariant and optimize from the baseline
steps: Clone node 1 and record mapping before visiting neighbors
Clone 2 and 4; recursive edges back to 1 reuse existing clone
All four nodes and their edges appear once in the resulting graph
dryRun: Clone node 1 and record mapping before visiting neighbors
Clone 2 and 4; recursive edges back to 1 reuse existing clone
All four nodes and their edges appear once in the resulting graph
solutions.interviewTip: Insert original->clone into the map before visiting neighbors to handle cycles and self-loops.

testCases.expected: clone has same adjacency but entirely new node identities
testCases.reason: A map connects each original node to its unique clone.

variants.name: Baseline idea
variants.explanation: Recreate nodes while walking each edge, but without a visited map cycles recurse forever.

variants.name: Optimized Java
variants.explanation: Clone node 1 and record mapping before visiting neighbors Clone 2 and 4; recursive edges back to 1 reuse existing clone All four nodes and their edges appear once in the resulting graph

solutions.title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
solutions.statement: Return grid coordinates from which water can flow downhill or flat to both Pacific and Atlantic borders.

example.explanation: Each listed cell can reach both oceans.

constraints: Follow the linked problem's input constraints and node definitions; verify edge cases as part of practice.
solutions.approach: Explain the invariant and optimize from the baseline
steps: Reverse the flow: initialize BFS from top/left Pacific border
Initialize another BFS from bottom/right Atlantic border
Walk only to equal/higher neighbors; intersect the two reachable grids
dryRun: Reverse the flow: initialize BFS from top/left Pacific border
Initialize another BFS from bottom/right Atlantic border
Walk only to equal/higher neighbors; intersect the two reachable grids
solutions.interviewTip: Reverse-searching from oceans avoids repeating DFS separately from each cell.

testCases.reason: Each listed cell can reach both oceans.

variants.name: Baseline idea
variants.explanation: Run a downhill path search from every grid cell to see which ocean borders are reachable.

variants.name: Optimized Java
variants.explanation: Reverse the flow: initialize BFS from top/left Pacific border Initialize another BFS from bottom/right Atlantic border Walk only to equal/higher neighbors; intersect the two reachable grids

solutions.title: Word Ladder
solutions.statement: Change one lowercase letter per step; every intermediate word must be in the dictionary. Return shortest sequence length.

example.explanation: hit->hot->dot->dog->cog has five words.

constraints: Follow the linked problem's input constraints and node definitions; verify edge cases as part of practice.
solutions.approach: Explain the invariant and optimize from the baseline
steps: Begin BFS layer 1 with hit
Generate hot at layer 2, dot/lot at layer 3, dog/log at layer 4
Reach cog at layer 5 -> return 5
dryRun: Begin BFS layer 1 with hit
Generate hot at layer 2, dot/lot at layer 3, dog/log at layer 4
Reach cog at layer 5 -> return 5
solutions.interviewTip: BFS guarantees the first endWord encountered uses the fewest transformations.

variants.name: Optimized Java
variants.explanation: Begin BFS layer 1 with hit Generate hot at layer 2, dot/lot at layer 3, dog/log at layer 4 Reach cog at layer 5 -> return 5

solutions.title: Course Schedule

companyEvidence.label: Reported in interview-prep coverage; not official company confirmation

solutions.statement: Return whether all courses can be finished, given prerequisite edges [course, prerequisite].

example.explanation: Course 0 must precede course 1.

constraints: Follow the linked problem's input constraints and node definitions; verify edge cases as part of practice.
solutions.approach: Explain the invariant and optimize from the baseline
steps: Build 0->1, indegree 0=0, indegree 1=1
Queue course 0, process it and release course 1
Process 1, seen 2 of 2 -> true
dryRun: Build 0->1, indegree 0=0, indegree 1=1
Queue course 0, process it and release course 1
Process 1, seen 2 of 2 -> true
solutions.interviewTip: A directed cycle leaves nodes with nonzero indegree, so fewer than n courses get processed.

variants.explanation: Try every permutation of courses and see if it satisfies all prerequisites.

variants.name: Optimized Java
variants.explanation: Build 0->1, indegree 0=0, indegree 1=1 Queue course 0, process it and release course 1 Process 1, seen 2 of 2 -> true

solutions.title: Course Schedule II
solutions.statement: Return any ordering of courses that respects prerequisites, or [] if a directed cycle exists.

example.explanation: Both sequences satisfy all edges.

constraints: Follow the linked problem's input constraints and node definitions; verify edge cases as part of practice.

steps: 0 has indegree 0, so it enters the output first

After both, course 3 becomes available; output valid four-course order

solutions.title: Redundant Connection
solutions.statement: An extra undirected edge was added to a tree. Return the last edge in input order creating a cycle.

example.explanation: The final edge connects two nodes already connected.

constraints: Follow the linked problem's input constraints and node definitions; verify edge cases as part of practice.
solutions.approach: Explain the invariant and optimize from the baseline
steps: Union (1,2), component {1,2}
Union (1,3), component {1,2,3}
Edge (2,3) has both roots equal -> cycle, return [2,3]
dryRun: Union (1,2), component {1,2}
Union (1,3), component {1,2,3}
Edge (2,3) has both roots equal -> cycle, return [2,3]
solutions.interviewTip: DSU cycle criterion: an edge is redundant exactly when its endpoints already share a root.

testCases.reason: The final edge connects two nodes already connected.

variants.name: Baseline idea
variants.explanation: For every edge, BFS the already-added graph to determine whether endpoints are connected.

variants.name: Optimized Java
variants.explanation: Union (1,2), component {1,2} Union (1,3), component {1,2,3} Edge (2,3) has both roots equal -> cycle, return [2,3]

solutions.title: Number Of Connected Components In An Undirected Graph
solutions.statement: Count connected components among n labeled vertices and undirected edges.

example.explanation: {0,1,2} and {3,4} are separate components.

constraints: Follow the linked problem's input constraints and node definitions; verify edge cases as part of practice.
solutions.approach: Explain the invariant and optimize from the baseline
steps: Begin with 5 singleton components
Union 0-1, 1-2 -> 3 groups
Union 3-4 -> 2 groups remain
dryRun: Begin with 5 singleton components
Union 0-1, 1-2 -> 3 groups
Union 3-4 -> 2 groups remain
solutions.interviewTip: DSU counts begin at n and decrease only when an edge connects two previously separate sets.

solutions.statement: Check whether n labeled nodes and undirected edges form one connected, acyclic tree.

Unions 0-1,0-2,0-3,1-4 all merge different components

solutions.title: Accounts Merge
solutions.statement: Merge accounts sharing email addresses (even transitively), returning name followed by sorted unique emails.

example.explanation: The two John accounts share johnsmith@mail.com.

constraints: Follow the linked problem's input constraints and node definitions; verify edge cases as part of practice.
solutions.approach: Explain the invariant and optimize from the baseline
steps: johnsmith@mail.com appears in two accounts, so union their email sets
Create groups by DSU root and sort each group's email addresses
Emit one John group and one independent Mary group
dryRun: johnsmith@mail.com appears in two accounts, so union their email sets
Create groups by DSU root and sort each group's email addresses
Emit one John group and one independent Mary group
solutions.interviewTip: Matching names alone do not imply accounts belong together; shared emails do.
